newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: LABOUR SAYS JOB SHARING WAY TO GO
The Federal Opposition says job sharing may be a way of helping more people find work.
Figures released yesterday ahow unemployment rose again in December, to a seasonally adjusted 8.6 percent.
Labor's Employment spokesman, Martin Ferguson suggested job sharing may be a way of reducing the unemployment rate.
He's told ABC Radio, the idea would tackle the challenge of trying to create more jobs in the context of more and more workers working longer hours, under more stress.
Hunter Valley gun buy-back going slow
In New South Wales, the Hunter Valley Alliance of Firearm owners says more than 90 percent of local gun owners still haven't surrended their weapons under the Federal Government's buyback scheme.
The Alliance's Bill Pearson says there's also been a bungle in the scheme's administration with people being over paid for the value of their weapons and some being paid twice for the same gun.
Mr Pearson says because there was no gun registration preceding the new legislation in New South Wales, he expects the majority of firearm owners will keep their weapons.
COMMONWEALTH LOWERS SOME LOAN RATES
Australia's biggest home-lender has tweaked its fixed mortgage rates a notch lower.
The Commonwealth Bank has announced a range of reductions in both owner-occupied and investment home loans.
Fixed rates for periods between two and five years are to fall by up to point-1-5 percent.
The Commonwealth Bank's Lyndell Fraser says a benefit has flowed from lower professional long-term rates ... based on the subdued inflation outlook.
PREMIER WELCOMES AUDIT OF GOVERNOR'S COSTS
The New South Wales Premier says he'd welcome the Auditor-General's assessment of the costs of moving the Governor out of Government House.
The Government says a predicted two-million-dollars in savings haven't been achieved, but rejects Opposition claims that the move has cost the state an extra one-piont-seven million dollars.
The Opposition says it will ask the Auditor-General, Tony Harris, for his advice on the matter.
But a spokesman for the Premier says he'd welcome an investigation.
FIVE ARRESTS FOLLOW CHAINING PROTEST
In northern New South Wales, police have arrested five people drug reform activists who chained themselves to police vehicles and a helicopter.
Members of the Police Rescue Squad used boltcutters to remove the demonstrators, who had chained themselves under four police vehicles at a Lismore Motel.
A fifth person was removed from a police helicopter in a paddock outside the city.
Those arrested were protesting over the annual helicopter drug raids carried out in northern New South Wales.
MAN IN STABLE CONDITION AFTER BEING SHOT BY POLICE
A 27-year-old man is in a stable condition in Royal Perth Hospital after being shot by police.
Police were called to a house in Rivervale about half past four yesterday afternoon, where they found a pregnant woman with stab wounds to the head and shoulder.
The man was standing nearby and was shot after failing to drop a knife.
The woman has also been admitted to hospital and its understood there are concerns about the foetus.
A Police internal investigation is underway.
ELLE SYNDICATE LOOKING FORWARD TO RACE
Director of Elle racing syndicate, John Harvey, says he's looking forward to the Whitbred round-the-world yacht race despite the current dispute and impounding of its training yacht.
The yacht was arrested and impounded in Sydney in a pay dispute with the former skipper of the all-female crew, Adrienne Cahalan.
Mr Harvey says the syndicate plans to charter a new vessel next week to continue training for the race which is due to start in September.
The yacht that will race in the Whitbread is still being built.
HIGH RATES OF CANCER IN WOLLONGONG
An investigation into a leukaemia cluster in Wollongong's industrial suburbs, has found unusually high rates of other cancers.
The Illawarra Public Health Unit is investigating the recent sudden increase in leukaemia cases among young people in the suburb of Warrawong.
Doctor Victoria Westley-Wise who is heading up the inquiry, says rates for other cancers, especially bladder cancer among men, are also higher than what would normally be expected.
She says bladder cancer's been linked to smoking and exposure to chemicals in the workplace.
AUSSIES IN TOURISM JOBS SUMMIT
Australia's tourism chiefs are among more than 120 of the world's leading tourism bosses attending a jobs summit in Portugal.
The three day conference is examining what action is needed by governments and industry to create millions of new jobs in the travel sector over the next decade.

The World Tourism and Travel Council will also present two new studies - one analysing the industry's contribution to worldwide employment and future potential - the other examining air transport liberalisation.
SOFT DRINK BOOM
Soft drink and milk consumption's up in Australia but the amount of beer being drunk has fallen again.
The Bureau of Statistics says soft drink consumption rose more than three percent, with Australians on average drinking more than 114 litres a year.
It's the fourth consecutive annual increase.
Beer consumption fell for the seventh successive year...to 95-and-a-half litres per person.
The bureau says Australians drink an average 104 litres of milk a year.
